notes.title: Introducing a New Reward: The Gift of the Eternal
notes.content:
Hello Dragon Hunters,

In our ongoing efforts to enhance player agency and reward progression, we'd like to introduce a new kind of reward: [b]Gift of the Eternal[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/f423dc4750a2a2118b2674757bec2f77661248cd.png[/img]

Our goal with that new reward is to provide meaningful choices that respect your time and investment in the game.

By allowing you to select rewards that align with your goals, we aim to enhance your gameplay experience and the feeling of overall progression.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/5ebb6693e846a1348cf79baad1c1591f778c2c16.png[/img]
[h3][b]What is a Gift of the Eternal?[/b][/h3]

Like any other equipment, fragments and ingredients, Eternal Gift drops on the ground.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/559477df79269ddd9c110cb4860acc9c0dec7019.png[/img]

Interacting with an Eternal Gift opens a window where you’ll be given a choice between the following options:
[list]
[*] Equipment: A weapon or armor piece,  randomly selected
[*] Ancestral Fragment: Random type and rarity
[*] Ingredients: A bundle of 20, randomly selected
[/list]
Additionally, you'll receive Experience Points for your character.

You have [b]2 rerolls[/b] available, allowing you to refresh your [b]3 rewards[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/7ad7c40ac842719448237aa885a9cc624a424aab.png[/img]
[i]Note: Once a selection is confirmed, it is final, and the chosen item will appear directly on the ground.[/i]

[h3][b]Where to find a Gift of the Eternal?[/b][/h3]

Gift of the Eternal can appear during the main storyline and endgame content.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/95c97c6feae0e2f8c152e65a7ad4aefe31639e65.png[/img]

[b]In the Story[/b]

Defeating major adversaries such as semi-bosses or bosses will grant you an Eternal Gift, acknowledging your accomplishments.​ Some key events also grant a guaranteed Eternal Gift.

[b]In Endgame Hunts[/b]

Each Hunt comprises multiple areas, and the total duration influences the number of potential Gift of the Eternal awarded. Longer, more challenging Hunts yield greater rewards.​

[b]In Dungeon Purifications[/b]

At the end of a Dungeon Purification, multiple chests appear. Based on your performance and progression within the dungeon, you increase your chances to obtain an Eternal Gift.​

[b]In the Test of Will[/b]
Your performance in the Test of Will determines the number of Gift of the Eternal you are guaranteed to receive upon completion. Higher tiers achieved equate to more Gifts.

For more details, please check our previous Devblog:
https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1863430/view/498319683381887030

[h3][b]Target farming by customizing your own Gift of the Eternal[/b][/h3]

To tailor Gift of the Eternal to your preferences, a dedicated customization tab is available on the Hunting Board.

Here, you can adjust parameters to influence the types of rewards offered, aligning them with your current objectives or build requirements.​

These customization options unlock progressively as you complete Hunts.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/28237cb0cbf47d4a2a355ef66a7739560b3fa14b.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/6e245927fff01255e6260a66d6f6ebfdb83e0332.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/d62f4d301d5b26eddda35e9101b7b08739ac616b.png[/img]

These options let you target farm deeper into what you’re looking for:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/9bf8209003c62ef4461e62259624cf6f69e26e52.png[/img]

[h2][b]Thanks for reading![/b][/h2]

Okay, that's all we have for this week.

Thanks again for all the support, it truly means a lot to us! Stay happy, stay healthy, and please remember to take good care of yourself. Enjoy the May day holidays if you have a day off and we’ll be back before you know it.

Sadly, you’ll have to wait just a tad longer before you can try the new features of The City and drop Gift of the Eternal. But worry not, we’ll have a huge Patch Notes ready for you to read in the few weeks, along with even more news to share!

See you next week!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/df5edd03500e88a5012160813c2f99ea24a3a01b.png[/img]

notes.title: Break into a new endgame activity: The Test of Will
notes.content:
[i]“Get ready to dive into your character’s psyche as they mentally prepare to face the voices of the dragons.”[/i]

Hello Dragon Hunters,

You may have already seen it on our roadmap, our next major update, [i]Nurõrgartt[/i], introduces a whole new endgame activity: [b]the Test of Will[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/ea3d58e134cd25d8a336592c24e98ae326f29e6c.png[/img]

In this mode, you'll face wave after wave of enemies while dealing with a mix of temporary buffs and debuffs, along with permanent bonuses that last throughout the run.

Each wave gets harder with stronger enemies, but the further you go, the better the rewards.

Whether you're coming back to Dragonkin after a break or just looking for your next challenge, the [i]Nurõrgartt[/i] update will be the perfect time to jump back in.

[h2][b]How does the Test of Will work?[/b][/h2]

The Test of Will is structured into [i]Trials[/i], each one made up of [b]10 waves of enemies[/b].
Your goal? Push as far as you can to unlock the best rewards possible!

Between each [i]Trial[/i], you’ll choose between [b]2 portals[/b]. Each one offers either a temporary buff or a permanent bonus that lasts for the rest of the Test of Will.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/341ff92ad0bb5ba2e70e071c4eacb1e4730ea2ec.png[/img]

At the start of each new Trial, enemies automatically gain +1 level and a random stat bonus. These effects stack as you progress into the Test of Will.

[h3][b]Temporary Bonuses[/b][/h3]

These effects only last for one [i]Trial[/i] (10 waves), but they have immediate impact.

Temporary bonuses are often powerful and perfect when the difficulty starts ramping up, or if you plan to leave the Test of Will at the end of this [i]Trial[/i].

Here are a few examples of temporary bonuses that may appear:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/9bb87892a0072790eafa46557121eb2a5968792a.png[/img]

[h3][b]Permanent Bonus[/b][/h3]

Permanent bonuses remain active until the end of your Test of Will run.

But to earn one, you’ll need to survive an entire [i]Trial[/i] while dealing with a temporary penalty, which can make that Trial especially challenging.

These bonuses are ideal if your goal is to push as far as possible.

Here are a few examples:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/b0f888514c5af81b91e894f812dde2094225a433.png[/img]

[h3][b]Special Waves[/b][/h3]

Each Trial includes [b]3 special waves[/b], appearing every 3 waves.

These waves introduce a gimmick that lasts for the duration of the wave. They’re designed to disrupt your rhythm and force you to adapt your strategy.

Here are a few examples:
[list]
[*] Large movement speed bonus for both characters and enemies
[*] Enemy group that continuously heals itself
[*] Toxic rain covering the entire arena
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/6dcbbed35e804890d71f2a0cc9a9d2764f28b6ae.png[/img]

[h3][b]Arena Maps[/b][/h3]

Each [i]Trial[/i] takes place on an arena map, with varied topography.

Some maps are more open, while others are tighter, with choke points that limit your movement and force you to rethink your approach to each wave.

A map can either work in your favor or be a disadvantage, so you’ll need to adapt accordingly.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/b24a062eaf065facd3c9bea83b66401b9f4b9707.png[/img]

[h3][b]Risk & Rewards[/b][/h3]

Starting from [i]Trial[/i] 3 (after 30 waves), you’ll have the option to exit the Test of Will between two Trials, securing all the rewards accumulated up to that point.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/df38648b8e5bb8f9686b7d5607a4e2b9d99a6bd0.png[/img]

When you finish the Test of Will, you’ll receive several rewards. Of course, the farther you go, the higher the loot quantity and quality:
[list]
[*] The final chest will contain more loot as you progress through the Trials.

[*] The rarity of items also increases: expect higher-quality loot, and greater chances of finding draconic or divine items.

[*] Each chest will contain at least one Gift of the Eternal, a new type of reward that we’ll explore more in an upcoming DevBlog.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/8cc0a19c0edbffe441c6c307e54baf8fa7045cbc.png[/img]

[b]As usual, you have a total of 6 deaths per session.[/b]

If you run out of lives, your attempt is considered a failure, and you’ll lose all the rewards accumulated up until that point.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/3866627a5921ebc315c163cb5d0768c654eca1c8.png[/img]

[b]Each wave requires you to defeat all enemies within a limited time.[/b]

Exceeding the time limit is considered a failure, and will immediately end your Test of Will.

[h2][b]That’s it for today![/b][/h2]

As always, if you encounter any bugs or have feedback to share, you can let us know through our Discord!

We also posted the results of the “Choose the Next Sneak Peek!” event on the server, along with some exclusive content in the #announcements channel. Be sure to check it out!

We hope you enjoy that new endgame activity, and thank you SO SO much for all the incredible support you've shown this game.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/df5edd03500e88a5012160813c2f99ea24a3a01b.png[/img]

notes.title: Eye on the new City Services and Features
notes.content:
Hello, Dragon Hunters,

Since the start of Early Access, we've been putting a significant amount of effort into improving [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1863430/view/506195274633317929][i]itemization[/i][/url] and specifically its flexibility, a core part of the gameplay experience that we know many of you have been eagerly awaiting.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/50f303ff0ecfebdfae036ff6b1adc21ab901f617.png[/img]

The [i]Nurõrgartt[/i] update introduces [b]5 new services[/b] to unlock in the City of Montescail, along with an entirely new storage system: [b]the Fragment Chest[/b].

These additions will give you greater flexibility and control when building your loadouts.

[h3][b]To sum up, here what you can expect:[/b][/h3]
[list]
[*] The Enchanter
[*] The Memorialist
[*] The Grand Benedictor
[*] The Artificer
[*] The Arsenal
[*] The Fragment Chest
[/list]
[h3][b]We are resetting City Points! [/b][/h3]

With the launch of these new features, we’ve decided to reset city points, allowing players to redistribute them freely.

This reset is also a great opportunity to fix any mistakes or experiment with a different upgrade path than the one previously selected.

[b]Please note:[/b]

This reset is not a feature, but a [b]one-time adjustment[/b] made specifically for the introduction of the new functionalities.

[b]This reset does not include the Abbey, the jailer, the Order, and the Pythia.[/b]

Without further ado, let’s deep dive into what’s coming.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/1177479afc23f3ed5031035c52bfdc26a96387b2.png[/img]
[h3][b]The Enchanter[/b][/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/ab7b7f2a9e51a090c7ce51c2ba3f68c7c87ae7e7.png[/img]

This new service allows you to modify one of the affixes on a piece of equipment or a “modifier” type hexagon on an ancestral fragment.

The Enchanter will reroll the selected affix or modifier, changing both its type and values.

After the first modification, the other affixes or hexagons will be locked, and only the enchanted affix or modifier can be rerolled again. 

[b]Please note:[/b]
[list]
[*] Rerolling a Divine affix or hexagon is guaranteed to retain the affix.
[*] [i]Draconic[/i] affixes cannot be modified/reroll.
[*] You have unlimited attempts, but each reroll increases the cost.
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/64f9ee57469d69ebd2b8f22c2d73d4ad23b83804.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/7de1441293288297e9ee82ff07bfde8560b96ca8.png[/img]

[h3][b]The Memorialist[/b][/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/30f1dad002e9a6b9dc4a111e7b78530456a9eab4.png[/img]

Visiting the Memorialist allows you to permanently [i]inscribe[/i] the bonus effect of a skill modifier, taken from a sacrificed skill fragment, onto a piece of equipment.

If a fragment contains multiple modifiers, the Memorialist will randomly select one from those present in the fragment.

The equipment then gains this bonus modifier for the associated skill, as long as it is equipped.

This allows you to benefit from a character or wyrmling skill modifier without having to place the fragment into the ancestral grid.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/a775d67ecf943b4aaeba3a145e8c31ed21bdf49c.png[/img]

[h3][b]The Grand Benedictor[/b] (anciently known as the Master of Scales)[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/cc4fac95cc2f0859b3e8cb0afa9a46283e2c554d.png[/img]

That new service enables you to manage your Codex of Talents and Skill Modifiers.

By sacrificing legendary and mythic items, as well as fragments of any rarity, you can permanently record bonuses within your Codex.

As your Codex fills up, you'll be able to select one talent and two modifiers from the skill of your choice.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/b8e7d1942139c1b9032d813697a16a917f196aa0.png[/img]

[h3][b]Artificer[/b][/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/8dc139acf56324210fc1acfe8e32ddf5ddf38b2c.png[/img]

That new service allows the transfer of draconic attributes from one piece of equipment to another.

[b]Please note:[/b]
[list]
[*] This process sacrifices the original piece of equipment.
[*] You can only transfer [i]Draconic[/i] affixes to a piece of equipment of the same type.
[*] This is the only way to obtain a Mythical Divine [i]Draconic[/i] item, as Mythical items do not drop with the [i]Draconic[/i] affixes.
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/d5830e8531dd0fd9775a21ec4ee12a5d08b8ff80.png[/img]

[h3][b]The Arsenal[/b][/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/72e72a3066bb6457711603f8aff33cb32ef44aed.png[/img]

This new feature allows you to save up to 4 build presets.

You can save your Equipment, including your currently equipped Wyrmling and its armor, but also your Attributes, the Grand Benedictor, and most importantly, your Ancestral Grid!

This new Service should let you experiment freely with different builds without the hassle or fear of losing your layouts.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/42e0dd0e1a152b157ce8673d36898137591d7468.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/1b226f65462c4f61e5d270b0bb18f49e4e1e0d87.png[/img]
[h3][b]Fragment Chest[/b][/h3]

Many players have expressed frustration over the limited storage space for Fragments and we've heard you! That’s why, in the upcoming update we introduce the Fragment chest!

You’ll now find several Fragment chests scattered throughout the city, right alongside the familiar Equipment chest.

Additionally, we're also adding another kind of chest type that provides quick access to the Arsenal.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/8319cd568ac1e2a074bb56ff46983eab71121e59.png[/img]

[h3][b]That’s it, for now![/b][/h3]

This wraps up our DevBlog on the upcoming City features.

We can’t wait for you to experience all these new Services!

As always, we’re eager to hear your thoughts on everything. You can expect more changes and adjustments throughout Early Access, as we hear your feedback on things.

If you want to have your say or keep up with all our news and updates, feel free to join our Discord or visit the Steam discussions! We do our best to reply to everyone and answer any questions you may have.

And yeah, we’ll keep saying it, but wishlisting our game helps us a ton. If you like our game, spread the word and let your friends know about Dragonkin: The Banished.

See you next week !

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/df5edd03500e88a5012160813c2f99ea24a3a01b.png[/img]

notes.title: Unveiling the Environments of Nurõrgartt
notes.content:
Hello, Dragon Hunters!

As the next major update for Dragonkin: The Banished approaches, we’d like to give you a sneak peek at the environments of [i]Nurõrgartt[/i] and the new Dragonkin you’ll have to face.

This new biome is defined by two distinct environments: the [b]tundra[/b] and [b]Fafnir’s glacier[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/bbccd0d9bfa4f3173c43518c19451acade15d602.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/d0fc2995a9389678a791793a85fee42df0b74398.png[/img]
[h3][b]The tundra[/b][/h3]

We love creating environments that are more than just backdrops for your adventure. Each of our levels offers the chance to discover, explore, and fight. The tundra of [i]Nurõrgartt[/i] is no exception.

While hunting in the tundra, you’ll come across the [i]Toriel Clan Village[/i], nestled within the fjords, which you can visit and explore.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/b25910603271f021b926513aa5b46a4572a931c6.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/7d42059ce4ff98e3102a202529f4a9cc7b7fd73d.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/c663d7722a1580a760d378b001f64743d42263c4.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/afc35511a968eed67cfce423fd49fb6b100bffa6.png[/img]

We designed the tundra’s mountainous plateaus as a cold, inhospitable land where life struggles to survive. Yet, here the Barbarians have managed to survive despite the influence of the White Dragon Lord, but they’re not alone…

[h3][b]The Walking Charnel[/b][/h3]

One of the most striking threats in this region is the Walking Charnel, a golem-like creature formed of fused armor and skeletons, bound together by ice. notes.title: How do we plan to handle updates during Early Access?
notes.content:
Hello Dragon Hunters,

It’s been 3 weeks since the Early Access launch! Thank you once again for joining us in this adventure.
We receive a great amount of feedback here on Steam but also on Discord.

We receive a great amount of feedback here on Steam but also on Discord. We’re trying our best to answer everyone but as you can guess, that’s not always possible. Though rest assured, we’re reading through every review, post, and discussion!

That's why we're writing this post, to let you know what we are currently working on and explain how we plan to handle updates during Early Access.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/e8d35efa1d067cfb0b8fe6233fcb3c6289b136c1.png[/img]
[h3][b]Patches & Updates[/b][/h3]

We're reading all the steam threads and your messages on Discord and currently fixing one issue after the other.

We believe that rather than trickling in small changes every few weeks, it’s more impactful to release [b]larger updates every 2-3 months.[/b]

This allows us :
[list]
[*] To take the time to properly evaluate player feedback and apply changes that truly improve the experience. That includes quality-of-life, bug fixes, and gameplay adjustments.

[*] Pack in enough content to make it worth returning to the game for another few dozen hours.

[*] And finally, work at a sustainable pace, giving us time to test everything properly before it goes live. We really don’t want to rush out half-baked patches just to hit a schedule.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/5a67537dd7f9fed26f2e513b6c0b0d25ce8b4f85.jpg[/img]
https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1863430/view/498314610455086374

[h3][b]Regarding Quality of Life features[/b][/h3]

During the playtests 3 months ago, for exemple, several players asked for a different camera. This feature was added into Dragonkin. We really want to continue incorporating feedback from our community into our updates.

Since launch there have been many things that players have found annoying or time consuming, as well as suggestions to improve general gameplay.

So we will try to address these one by one.

[list]
[*] Better visibility of important Fragments and Equipment on the ground.
[i](Such as indicators to show whether a character/wyrmling skill is associated with the Fragment. And indicators to show if a drop is Divine, Draconic if not both.)[/i]

[*] A dedicated chest in town for Fragments (we know you've been asking for it).

[*] The addition of guides and tooltips as well as improving existing ones.

[*] A notification to alert the player when city XP is earned.
[i](Such as when the player collects relics)[/i] 

[*] The ability to share currencies and materials between characters in the same city.

[/list]
Many players have expressed the wish to [b]save their Ancestral Grid[/b].

This feature will be introduced alongside the Arsenal, allowing you to save preset configurations of your Ancestral Grid but also everything regarding your character (equipment, attributs, passives, wyrmling, etc…), making experimentation much easier.

Additionally, many features are planned for the crafting system, such as the ability to modify an equipment, or transferring Draconic Corruption from one draconic item to another.

These will be gradually introduced over future updates.

For more information regarding this topic, please check: https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1863430/view/506195274633317929

[h3][b]How about critical bugs?[/b][/h3]

If a major game-breaking bug / Blocker bug shows up, we’ll push an emergency fix as soon as possible (like we did recently for quest issues).

For standard balance tweaks and minor fixes, we’ll roll those into the larger updates.

[h3][b]What are the major points we want to work on and address?[/b][/h3]

Here are some key areas we believe require significant updates to address:
[list]
[*] Lack of impact or weight behind skills.

[*] Balance issues with character skills, with some being too weak and others too powerful.

[*] Progression balance is off.

[*] Enemies populations are not dense enough.

[*] Optimization.
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/7ba68774fbf4b816db753fa3d505b27b8bc2d1e4.png[/img]
[h3][b]A Message From Us[/b][/h3]

Thank you for all of your kind words, support, and love since we announced the start of our Early Access! We still have a long way to go!

As a small team that has been working on this game for several years, it makes us so happy to see players enjoy the game. From the bottom of our hearts, we truly appreciate all the love and support you have shown us.

[h3][b]Your feedback helps![/b][/h3]

Keep sending us your feedback - we love to see it, and are listening! We're committed to making Dragonkin: The Banished the best game it can be at our scale.

As always, for any in-game issues/bugs, please report any bugs here on Steam, or in our Discord! All reports are much appreciated, as we continue to work on bug-fixing!

Thanks for being part of this adventure!

notes.title: More about the Itemization - Dragonkin: The Banished DevBlog
notes.content:
Hello, dragon hunters!

We hope you’ve been enjoying your time in the demo for Dragonkin: The Banished. The demo is available until March 3rd, so if you haven’t tried it out yet, don’t miss the opportunity. 

During the [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1863430/view/508445806184891240]Montescail City DevBlog[/url], we briefly mentioned Itemization, and many of you had questions, especially on Discord. So today, we’re diving into the details.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/6e4b7953812c6253f949131d27787d0fe60b4c8f.png[/img]

If you haven’t read our [url=url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1863430/view/508444538590724447]Ancestral Grid DevBlog[/url], it’s worth checking out, as it directly ties in to what we are going to cover.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/fde4d766b3ce33a8e90d0a208bca8325e4e30fb3.png[/img]
[h3][b]Loot & Rarities[/b][/h3]

Throughout the game, you will be able to obtain weapons, armor, as well as fragments of different rarities. It goes without saying that the higher the rarity, the more powerful the items will be.
[list]
[*] [b]Common, Uncommon, Rare, Legendary, Mythical[/b]
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/607c2fa4eb95abea64d07ca8888f9139a4fe55bf.png[/img]

For equipment including weapons, armor and rings, a higher rarity offers more powerful statistics, better scaling based on the item level, and above all, additional affixes.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/65b023c3d94f0941124d2ddc3122526031416708.png[/img]

Regarding fragments, a higher rarity means potentially larger and more complex fragments. These also have more power to reach milestones more easily.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/c0628de05137b5ccf692ba58e2fe363fe0623cf0.png[/img]

Pendants are always Mythical and exclusive to endgame content.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/64dd8824ba573712b22c9272a6d35e7fbb87ab1c.png[/img]

In addition to rarities, certain equipment or fragments may present variations with particular characteristics and appear as Divine and/or Draconic drops. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/e914cb031c1533fc42c91c20414bee767b4808a1.png[/img]
[h3][b]Divine[/b][/h3]
Any gear can be divine regardless of its base rarity. These items benefit from notable improvements and appear from Calamity I difficulty, the penultimate difficulty tier in Dragonkin.
[list]
[*] A piece of divine armor/weapon has a max quality affix with +25% enhancement.

[*] A divine potion has a maximized and enhanced potion effect of 25%.

[*] A divine fragment has a modifier at the maximum rank relative to its rarity, the effectiveness of which is increased by 2.

[*] A Wyrmling armor at rank 10 is considered divine.
[/list]
Regarding the divine pendants, we will tell you more about these in the future.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/376872770a8bf3d9d5a78e320dfd96eb94799c7e.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/558e2f7ea13777c97f2ed2c6e004a3fabecbce0c.png[/img]
[h3][b]Draconic[/b][/h3]

Draconic equipment offers particularly powerful statistics, but never comes without cost. Every Draconic item provides two bonuses alongside a penalty.

There are [b]3 ranks of dragon corruption[/b] with progressive values, which require playing at higher difficulties.

[i]Note: fragments cannot be Draconic.[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/01b32d50161a337ef3c08c96554801a496cb8aad.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/2271d8bc2aa9a8ca806e3859bbca96f47b37a9c9.png[/img]
[h3][b]Divine and Draconic[/b][/h3]
Finally, an item can be both Divine and Draconic, which you can guess will be a goal when building your characters. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/a02bfa15c4c1182ef2f279c99afe056b814fd9b6.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/01272609ee26d5fbf86c48357187a163fa83232a.png[/img]
[h3][b]Talents[/b][/h3]

We have already mentioned talents several times, especially with pendants.

Each character has a list of talents. These talents are divided into 3 ranks, each requiring a certain number of points to activate.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/c8676ce4fc3f8446df2c4bb7ce532b2cbf974662.png[/img]

Among the universal talents, each class has unique talents that only it can acquire. These talents can appear on legendary or mythic weapons and armor, but not on crafting rings or primordial pendants, which remain universal.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/0c85d193be7fe6f17b25ae9ee5d17221bcb5a395.png[/img]

[h3][b]How to get Talent points?[/b]
[/h3]
ou can get them in several ways:

[b]From looting[/b]
[list]
[*] Legendary and Mythic gear give 1 and 2 points to a random talent, respectively.
[*] A primordial pendant, obtained in endgame content, gives 2 points to a random talent.
[/list]
[b]From crafting[/b]

Crafting allows you to customize items your way, based on the materials you obtain. The goal is to give players more control over theorycrafting.
[list]
[*] A legendary or mythical ring allows you to choose a talent to strengthen during its creation.
[*] Armor ornaments provide points in a specific talent, selectable from four options.
[*] The Scale Master extracts talents from equipment to allow you to select one from those unlocked.
[/list]
[b]From Wyrmling's armor[/b]
[list]
[*] Wyrmling armor can improve a specific and unique talent.
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/d75c5c8ed4e26ea710ed51e501e8ba783c8f8da3.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/e891c62a339878df055165a817b762029c9dc937.png[/img]
[h3][b]Crafting[/b][/h3]

As part of our city blog, we noted that there are several Buildings and Services from which you can upgrade and build your loadouts.

[b]The Jeweler[/b]
[list]
[*] At the Jeweler you can create rings with predefined stats and talents.
[*] Can be produced Divine.
[/list]
[b]The Apothecary[/b]
[list]
[*] The apothecary allows you to create potions with various unique effects. The max level of these potions is Divine.
[*] Can be produced Divine.
[/list]
[b]The Jailer[/b]
[list]
[*] It allows you to craft and then improve Wyrmling armor to personalize the statistics and talents granted by your companion. You can also switch out your Wyrmlings at the Jailer. 
[/list]
[b]The Ornamentalist[/b]
[list]
[*] The Ornamentalist allows you to add ornaments to your armor pieces to obtain specific talent points.
[/list]
[b]The Enchanter[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/cd77934d433cb31447ba5e04966ff008953fc5ff.png[/img]
[list]
[*] The Enchanter allows you to modify a piece of armor and/or a weapon, by rerolling ONE affix of your choice.
[*] It also allows you to randomly reforge 1 hexagon (2 for mythicals) on a fragment. It is thus possible to change and adjust your skill modifiers.
[/list]
[b]The Master of Scales[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/cd77934d433cb31447ba5e04966ff008953fc5ff.png[/img]
[list]
[*] The Master of Scales allows you to manage a codex of talents and skill modifiers, requiring the sacrifice of legendary and mythic equipment, including fragments. A well-filled codex allows you to benefit from sacrificed bonuses without even having the equipment or fragments equipped.
[/list]
[b]The Artificer[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/cd77934d433cb31447ba5e04966ff008953fc5ff.png[/img]
[list]
[*] The Artificer allows the transfer of draconic corruption from one Draconic object to another infinitely.
[/list]
[b]The Memorialist[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/cd77934d433cb31447ba5e04966ff008953fc5ff.png[/img]
[list]
[*] The Memorialist allows you to register a skill modifier from a sacrificed fragment in a piece of equipment, in order to benefit from its bonus without having to place it in the ancestral grid.
[/list]
[h3][b]That's it, for now[/b][/h3]

[b]This concludes our DevBlog on itemization.[/b]

That was quite a lot to discuss and we can’t wait for you to experience all of these systems in Early Access.

As always, keep checking our Steam page and come take a look at our Discord server! We are here every day to collect your opinions and answer questions.

See you soon!

notes.title: Tips and Tricks for getting the most out of the Dragonkin Demo!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/6b426903b98184b8831b30f513b9965c24185299.png[/img]
Hello hunters! 

We hope you’ve been enjoying your first look at Dragonkin: The Banished via the demo released as part of Steam Next Fest. 

There are a lot of differences between the Demo and the Early Access planned for March 6th, but from the feedback we’ve received so far, we’ve learned a lot. We’re still seeing what we’re able to do in the short term regarding this, but in the meantime we wanted to introduce some general tips and advice for getting the most out of the Dragonkin: the Banished Demo! 

[h3]Prologue[/h3]

The demo starts with the prologue. This is a cinematic experience designed to introduce you to the characters, gameplay, story and the world. During this section, there’s no mini-map, inventory or character customization. It’s designed to give you a feel for each of the characters, but if you prefer, you can skip the prologue by pressing the esc key and choosing the skip option.

[h3]Ancestral Grid Advice[/h3]

In the demo, you have access to 3 characters at level 35. We understand that some players would prefer to start their experience at level 1. Of course, this is the experience in Early Access where you’ll start at level 1 and be able to play through the 1st act of Dragonkin and keep leveling via the various end-game content.

For the demo, we wanted to give players the tools to experiment and play around with the systems by creating preset builds. These are examples of what these characters can be, they’re by no means perfect, nor are they the optimal build for every player's playstyle. There is room for experimentation and growth, this is one of the core loops of Dragonkin. 

As you do dungeon purification runs, you’ll collect new fragments. These can be used to change and empower your skills by altering the layout of your Ancestral Grid. We recommend getting used to your character and their skills before you start to experiment with the Ancestral Grid.

We know that there’s more we could have done with the demo to assist in explaining the Ancestral Grid system, it wasn’t our intention to drop players in at the deep end. Ideally, we wanted to give players the tools needed to explore the depth of the Ancestral Grid system without the need for a significant time investment in levelling your character. We know we missed the mark somewhat with this, but hope you will give the demo a shot. 

If you wish to reset your character to how they were at the start of the beta, you can find the default builds below:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/4d9e57c0d77865d0121fe5212100dcf3bb965eea.png[/img]
[h3]Camera Options + Control options[/h3]

You can adjust your gameplay experience in the Dragonkin: The Banished. You can play Dragonkin with either a keyboard and mouse or a controller. For those playing on keyboard, you can choose between mouse movement or keyboard movement. 

Additionally, we have two camera modes: action and classic mode. Action is the default in Dragonkin, but if you’d prefer to draw the camera back a little, we’d recommend playing in classic mode. You can find this setting in the options menu under UI. 

[h3]General Advice for getting the most out of the Dragonkin Demo: [/h3][list][*] You can instantly teleport around the city by opening the city menu by pressing the R key to visit the different vendors and merchants
[*] You can create custom rings and potions at the Jeweler and the Apothecary
[*] You can adjust your attributes in the character menu
[*] For players who want to deep dive into the Ancestral Grid you can experiment with different Wrymlings (You can change Wrymlings at the Jailer). [list][*] Wyrmling abilities can vastly alter your playstyle, so don’t forget to update your Ancestral Grid! (Recommended for players who have gotten used to the systems in Dragonkin)
[/list][/list]
Thank you for joining us in the Demo. We’re excited for you to experience even more content when Dragonkin: The Banished comes to Early Access on March 6th. 

If you want to follow our progress then don’t forget to wishlist the game!

notes.title: Dragonkin: The Banished DEMO known issues
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/b222114be912604ad74535e521abe015216e4c40.png[/img]
Hello Dragon Hunters!

Many of you have already tried our demo, and we sincerely thank you for that.

For a small number of players, we have noted some specific issues that cause issues with the demo, so we wanted to share what we've found out.

[h3]Crashes[/h3]
[list][*]The most significant issue is a crash affecting players using 13th and 14th-generation Intel CPUs, particularly in games running on Unreal Engine 5, which uses Oodle for data decompression. You can find more details about this specific issue [url=https://www.radgametools.com/oodleintel.htm]here[/url]. For full transparency, this issue affects approximately 0.8% of our players.[*]Another cause of crashes is the use of RivaTuner Statistics Server (RTSS), which is commonly used with MSI Afterburner. This module injects rendering code for its overlay display. Unfortunately, we are not the only game affected, and this issue impacts about 0.4% of our players. Turning off MSI Afterburner should resolve this issue.[*]The last type of crash identified affects players using an AMD 7900XT/XTX graphics card. As of today, we have not yet determined the exact cause of the issue and are actively investigating. This affects approximately 0.2% of players.[/list]
[h3]Low Texture Quality in 4K[/h3]
Some players have reported texture quality issues when playing the game at 4K resolution. We have identified the problem and should have it resolved for the Early Access launch on March 6. 

In the meantime, for the demo, playing at a lower resolution (2K) should resolve the issue for affected players. However, keep in mind that if you are playing in borderless windowed mode, the game will still use your monitor’s native resolution. Changing the resolution in the game's graphics options won’t have any effect in this mode (to clarify this for players, resolution options will be removed when playing in borderless windowed mode at EA launch).

We are doing everything we can to ensure the best possible Early Access launch. We want to thank the players who helped us identify these issues, allowing us to work on fixing them.

Thank you all, and happy hunting!

The Eko Software Team

notes.title: A step into the City of Montescail - Dragonkin: The Banished DevBlog
notes.content:
[i]“Built in the heart of the mountains, sheltered from Dragons and their voices, lies a huge city and bastion of humanity.”[/i]

Hello Dragon Hunters!

This time, we’re bringing something special to the table, as we finally unveil one of the most important aspects of Dragonkin: The Banished ; [b]The city of Montescail[/b].

But before that, we're excited to reveal that we're going to launch a demo for Dragonkin: The Banished on February 20th.

But back to the topic at hand, welcome to Montescail!

[previewyoutube=MmPn8euZspk;full][i][link of the video][/i][/previewyoutube]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/7291c5f9c18ca244ee97f8d3e451ae883c396a44.png[/img]
[h3][b]Multiple Heroes, One Town[/b][/h3]

If you read our previous [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1863430/view/508445172204306551][b]DevBlog that featured the single-player and multiplayer[/b][/url], you already know that before you create your first character, you’ll need to create an offline or online city or simply join a friend's existing online city.

If you want more details on how multiplayer works, please check our previous DevBlog:

https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1863430/view/508445172204306551

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/c6d5b0de542d65ffa980d6f1c654a2b441de7f73.png[/img]

Not only, Montescail contains various buildings that allow the player to craft various potions, train against dummies, manage their Wyrmlings, and much more, this city also serves as a hub for all characters created within it.

Each character has access to a [b]Personal Chest[/b], a private storage space where you can put your equipment.

All characters tied to the same city have access to a [b]Shared Chest[/b], a storage where you can put the equipment you gathered during your adventure.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/166d953a2393cfe6deb1c745826692a60a71ea79.png[/img]

Each character in the city benefits from the improvements and features unlocked within that city. With the group system, independent of your characters, you can progress the story or endgame hunts alone, together simultaneously, asynchronously, or even across different characters.

[h3][b]A City That Evolves With You[/b][/h3]

The city of Montescail is divided into several districts, each representing a unique civilization from the world, Montescail will evolve alongside your characters.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/07aa71b6917e9fd79f7bd995c6cca5ff82b80a47.png[/img]

The more you progress in the story or complete endgame content, the more [b]Prosperity (XP)[/b] you earn. Each time your city levels up, you receive [b]City Upgrade Points[/b], which can be spent to unlock and enhance Services and Buildings. These upgrades improve the efficiency of Services, grant passive bonuses to your heroes, and sometimes unlock unique perks.

Though you'll need to prioritize which aspects to focus on, you'll have the opportunity to unlock everything as you progress.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/5019258e366f0d38af2f3c4326e743d3f8fefa5c.png[/img]

[h3][b]So, what exactly can you do in Montescail?[/b][/h3]

You will unlock a wide variety of merchants, each offering unique Services. This can be as simple as a [b]Dark Merchant[/b] to buy items or sell your junk, a [b]Memorialist[/b] to modify your equipment pieces, an [b]Ornamentalist[/b] to craft ornaments for each armor type, an [b]Arsenal[/b] allowing you to save and change your equipment presets.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/da14d3bf915bbe6339d10d90692dc7a5a29cfb40.png[/img]

You can also unlock [b]various perks[/b] such as larger city storage, experience bonuses, damage, movement speed or even additional slots for your Ancestral Grid.

Green indicates upgrades you have already unlocked, while yellow show upgrades that are available but require City Upgrade Points to be unlocked. Some buildings have prerequisites that must be met to reveal the next bonus and unlock further upgrades.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/cb558a6d31cec2fa309936b73832402d3cfe6c29.png[/img]

Here an exemple with the [b]Jeweler[/b] able to craft rings.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/0978f25515b3e5d2aa822c9c4603321cbf02192c.png[/img]

You can customize your ring by always selecting the desired attribute between courage, Intellect, Resilience, and Agility, followed by a primary (offensive) stat such as Cooldown Reduction, Life Drain, Summon Damage, then a secondary stat (defensive), such as Maximum HP, Barrier, or X Resistance.

As the ring's rarity increases, the values of these stats improve. Additionally, starting at Legendary rarity, you gain the ability to improve your ring further by adding a talent, which can stack with your itemization:

[list]
    [*]Common: 1 attribute + 2 stats
    [*]Uncommon: 1 attribute + 2 stats
    [*]Rare: 1 attribute + 2 stats
    [*]Legendary: 1 attribute + 2 stats + 1 Talent (1 point)
    [*]Mythic: 1 attribute + 2 stats + 1 random stats + 1 Talent (2 points)
[/list]
You may wonder what the [b]Talents[/b] are!  In short, these are earned and obtained via a points system. Each talent has several ranks with stacking effects and some even offer exclusive bonuses at the highest rank. You’ll get to know more in a dedicated DevBlog that covers itemization.

Now let's talk about the [b]Apothecary[/b] to create special healing potions.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/592655e66cda6e6abbb5069714085d3d0b43e9f2.png[/img]

Here, you can customize your potion by first selecting the desired effect(s). The rarity of the potion determines the amount of healing it provides and the number of effects you can add:

[list]
    [*]Common: No additional effects.
    [*]Uncommon: Adds 1 effect
    [*]Rare: 2 effects
    [*]Legendary: 3 effects
    [*]Mythic: 3 effects + 1 random effect
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/eca113588078c6328a333d01114b15878a9ef57a.png[/img]

All these services and perks are meant to participate in the improvement of your character and itemization as much as possible.

[h3][b]A city that visually changes as you progress[/b][/h3]

Montescail evolves visually with every improvement, each building subtly transforms as you upgrade them. Upgrading a merchant enhances their shop, improving the training camp introduces new types of mannequins, and unlocking certain Services result in the development of entire streets. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/3ba0942159ef55eef3e491c7c24190389a4e4dea.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/05884a1c5c6dbeda69cf55cc5f5ef6724719d645.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/940c8614244dc60506dc575478d80e62eccaadc5.png[/img]

[h3][b]For the players that participate in our Early Access[/b][/h3]

You will have access to [b]exclusive customization[/b] options for Montescail. Here is a sneak peak of one of the city customization we plan to add at the Early Access launch.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/b85e519717aee50e796ba8617b8921869b9c14b2.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/6545ae99b71d76cefabe7af3e126eb10c6192f15.png[/img]

To give you a bit of behind-the-scenes insight, our Environment Artist, Pierre, wanted to share with you more about his design process and how he shaped the look and feel of this exclusive Early Access customization DLC:

[quote=author][i]“Hi, my name is Pierre Huot, and I've been an Environment Artist at Eko Software for three years now. I've worked on several in-game environments, including the game's main hub, the city of Montescail.

For this first customization DLC, my inspiration came from imagining how the people of Montescail would celebrate and honor the heroes who sealed the Rift decades ago, preventing one of the dragons, Saur Iknog, from coming back.

The main idea was to decorate the city with various elements, such as banners, statues, and rooftops using a palette of white and gold, along with a unique color for each district. White symbolizes unity and neutrality among Montescail’s diverse inhabitants, while gold represents the Eternal Scales, central artifacts in the Dragonkin story that hold deep significance in each culture.

That said, I also wanted to highlight the individuality of each district through certain details, particularly the statues. Their styles and symbolism are more closely tied to the experiences of each civilization and how they perceived the great Rift War against Saur Iknog."[/i][/quote]

[h3][b]Navigating Montescail with Ease[/b][/h3]

Given the vast size of the city, we understand that walking between the different buildings can take some time. That’s why we’ve designed a system to help you quickly access all of the city’s key locations and services. Just open the menu and click where you want to go, you’ll be able to move instantly between districts or interact directly with the merchant or store you want to engage with.

As we wrap up this DevBlog, some of the features displayed will be implemented throughout Early Access.

We are interested to know which aspects of the town caught your interest. Share your thoughts in the comments or hop onto our Discord server to discuss with our team!

As usual, stay tuned for more updates and reveals about our game consider adding Dragonkin: The Banished to your wishlist.

And don't forget next week, you'll be able try Dragonkin: The Banished when our demo drops on February 20th.

notes.title: Frequently Asked Questions - Dragonkin: The Banished
notes.content:
Hello Dragon Hunters,
As you know, Dragonkin: The Banished will launch in Early Access on March 6th.

No doubt, you’ve got questions. Well, we’ve got answers! We’ll be updating our FAQ before and throughout Early Access in response to any questions you may have.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/225592faf069f2365fe850f8a6715b35591d13b7.png[/img]

Don’t forget, you can submit your questions to our development team directly on our Discord or over in the Steam Discussions. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/67f55c6598469dee46fd421ac5aec876984237ef.png[/img]
[h2][b]Frequently Asked Questions[/b][/h2]


[h3][b]What type of game is Dragonkin: The Banished ?[/b][/h3]

Dragonkin: The Banished is a Hack’N’Slash ARPG, set in a universe where humanity lives under the fear of Dragons. Trying to now escape the place they were banished to, these creatures corrupt minds with their voices or leave permanent scars on the land with their blood shaping the world of Dragonkin: The Banished.

[h3][b]Will Dragonkin: The Banished release on other platforms? [/b][/h3]

Yes, after the Early Access has ended, we’ll be releasing Dragonkin: The Banished on other platforms (including console) with all the updates, changes, and additions that will have been made throughout the Early Access.

[h3][b]Is Dragonkin compatible with Steam Deck? [/b][/h3]

We’re working to ensure that the game works on Steam Deck. We’ll be submitting the Early Access build for review to ensure compatibility. Expect to hear more closer to EA launch on March 6th. 

[h3][b]Why is Dragonkin: The Banished coming out in Early Access?[/b][/h3]

Dragonkin: The Banished will launch on Steam Early Access so that players can experience all the game already has to offer, as we work towards the full release, we’ll be using as much as we can player feedback into our updates to make the game the best it can be at full release.

However, the best part of being in Early Access is that it’s a collaborative process. We know how passionate the Hack’N’Slash community is and we want to use that feedback to finetune and improve the game. Lastly, Early Access allows us to invest more into the development of the game, giving us the room to expand beyond what we have planned in our roadmap. 

If you want to read our full thoughts on Early Access, check out our [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1863430/view/508442816334004686]DevBlog on the topic[/url]!

[h3][b]When does Early Access start? [/b][/h3]

Dragonkin: The Banished will enter Early Access on March 6th. We’ll share the exact launch time in different regions closer to EA launch.

[h3][b]Where can I play Dragonkin in Early Access?[/b][/h3]

During Early Access, Dragonkin will only be playable via Steam.

[h3][b]How much will Dragonkin: The Banished cost in Early Access?[/b][/h3]

Dragonkin: The Banished will be priced at €24.99€/$24.99$/£20.99 at Early Access launch. We’ll also be running a 20% off campaign at launch, so there will be an extra saving for early adopters. 

Any potential price increase at the full release will be determined at a later time.

[i]Note: price may vary depending on your region.[/i]

[h3][b]Will there be Microtransactions in Dragonkin: The Banished? [/b][/h3]

Microtransactions and in-game purchases are not part of Dragonkin’s design. Dragonkin will never be a pay-to-win or pay-to-progress-faster.

During early access, we will be giving cosmetics that will be exclusive to early access owners. After the full release, paying cosmetics and/or DLCs may be added if we think they might be of interest to players as well as free updates.

[h3][b]How long will Dragonkin: The Banished be in Early Access?[/b][/h3]

We expect Dragonkin: The Banished to remain in Early Access for around one year, with regular updates and new content planned along the way. We’ll be sharing our roadmap shortly, so stay tuned for that!

[h3][b]What is in Dragonkin: The Banished Early Access?[/b][/h3]

We’ve built a solid foundation for the launch of Early Access, this includes a prologue, the chapter one of the story, the city of Montescail, [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1863430/view/516325296815734848]3 playable heroes[/url], 4 wyrmlings acting as character specialization and endgame content to keep players busy as they build out their [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1863430/view/508444538590724447]Ancestral Grid[/url] and while we’re working on the next update.

We also have a roadmap for things we have planned to bring into the game during Early Access, such as a 4th hero, extra character skills, more end game content, [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1863430/view/508445172204306551]multiplayer[/url] and more…

[h3][b]Is Dragonkin: The Banished playable in multiplayer?[/b][/h3]

Multiplayer is planned, and we’ve been working on it for a while. For the development of Dragonkin, we switched to a new engine. We’ve been working on the multiplayer implementation for a while now, and will continue to do so throughout early access. This feature will be rolled out in one of our future updates.

[url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1863430/view/508445172204306551]Check our DevBlog dedicated on multiplayer[/url] if you want more information.

[h3][b]Is Dragonkin: the Banished always-online? [/b][/h3]

Dragonkin: the Banished is not always-online. Dragonkin is designed to be fully playable offline whenever and wherever you want. This will be true even after multiplayer co-op is introduced.

We have planned some shared elements, your city state for example. But for those who prefer to hunt alone, you will be able to enjoy Dragonkin: The Banished completely independent and without the influence of any other players if you wish.

You will, of course, still receive all the updates and improvements we will bring to the game throughout its development.

[h3][b]Can I stream or make content about Dragonkin? [/b][/h3]

You are free to make content or stream the game. We appreciate the thought and look forward to seeing what the community creates.

[h3][b]Is MyNacon Necessary? [/b][/h3]

MyNacon is not required to play Dragonkin, if you do not wish to make an account, skip the process when opening the game. If you wish to opt-in later, you can sign up on the MyNacon website. 

MyNacon offers you special discounts on all of Nacon’s products and games. You can also stay up-to-date with Dragonkin and your favorite games with the latest news.

[h3][b]How are you planning on involving the Community in the development process?[/b][/h3]

As you may know, we recently invited players to participate in a closed playtest! 

In a similar vein, throughout Early Access, we will sometimes conduct surveys on our Discord server. We’ll also have dedicated channels where players can share their feedback directly. You may have also noticed that we’re regularly monitoring the Steam forums. 

We’re eager to take as many opportunities to interact and collect feedback from the community. Ensuring that no matter where you leave your feedback, your voices are heard!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/a6b66dba8699b4b4a5e485956af3015608c33ce7.png[/img]

[h2][b]Thank you for supporting Dragonkin: The Banished![/b][/h2]

Your encouragement really motivates us to go forward as we continue to work on Dragonkin.
As always, we invite you to follow us on social media, join our Discord, and check out our Steam page for the latest news and updates.

notes.title: How Singleplayer & Multiplayer works and when to expect Multiplayer in EA
notes.content:
Hello everyone,

We’d like to provide you with more details about the single and multiplayer modes in Dragonkin: The Banished, the latter of which will be added as an update during Early Access.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/88d194f76f8957f7dd1d8f5c6dbc4a39203bc67e.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/d369f09fc0baeb50f5b7ca9ef7f8d47dae2b7e35.png[/img]
[h3][b]About Single-Player[/b][/h3]

Dragonkin is designed to be fully playable offline whenever and wherever you want. This will be true even after multiplayer co-op is introduced. 

We have planned some shared elements, your city state for example. But for those who prefer to hunt alone, you will be able to enjoy Dragonkin: The Banished completely independent and  without the influence of any other players if you wish.  

You will, of course, still receive all the updates and improvements we will bring to the game throughout its development.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/14b33a7bdafb23abf20211ce1f1b9a6d9e5d3167.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/ea2edf058e153fcb43e13c92a61934a44c912313.png[/img]
[h3][b]About Multiplayer[/b][/h3]

Now, let's talk multiplayer! 

Multiplayer is planned, and we’ve been working on it for a while. For the development of Dragonkin, we switched to a new engine. We’ve been working on the multiplayer implementation for a while now, and will continue to do so throughout early access. This feature will be rolled out in one of our future updates (you’ll learn more about the release window when we publish our roadmap).

Here are some details about what we’re planning:

[list]
    [*][b]Online multiplayer:[/b] With up to 4 players cooperating online and hunting dragons, either through the story or in endgame hunts.
    [*][b]Montescail City:[/b] A shared hub where you’ll meet your friends and develop the city together. The number of friends who can share a city is still to be defined.
    [*][b]Couch co-op:[/b] The local two-player co-op mode will be available upon the full release of the game. You’ll be able to play couch co-op both offline and online, and you can join other players only if your characters were created in an online city.
    [*][b]Matchmaking:[/b] It will be possible to play with other hunters online by temporarily joining a city or inviting them to yours. As a guest, you won’t directly benefit from the improvements of the city you visit, but from your own city’s upgrades, which will continue to evolve.

[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/781dbc4484c2a1da0b0f2e80a332d110f8311e8c.png[/img]

[h3][b]Offline mode and online mode[/b][/h3]

Before you create your first character, you’ll need to create or join a friend's existing online city. If you create one, you’ll have to choose whether your city, Montescail, will be in offline or online mode. You can create up to [b]8 characters per player in each city[/b], but you can also create multiple cities, both offline and online. 

This hub serves as the operational base for all characters created within it. Meaning that each character in the city benefits from the improvements and features unlocked within that city. With the group system, independent of your characters, you can progress the story or endgame hunts alone, together simultaneously, asynchronously, or even across different characters.

[b]An offline city does not require an internet connection. It’s designed for those who prefer a solo and/or local co-op experience.[/b]

[b]Beware:[/b] A character or city created offline will not be able to join the online game, and this choice is final. However, we are considering the possibility, in the future, of transferring your cities and characters from online mode to offline mode.

An online city requires a constant internet connection. It’s designed for those who prefer to play with other hunters or friends online.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/fcc6b74c9bb92ef7f70d7294f6a8843d6a8f145c.png[/img]
[list]
    [*]You can play Dragonkin: The Banished offline whenever you want, without an internet connection, even after the multiplayer mode arrives.
    [*]Multiplayer is coming and will be rolled out in one of our future Early Access updates.
    [*]Couch co-op is coming and will be available at the full release of the game.
[/list]
[h3][b]Development is progressing well, and the next steps are coming soon[/b][/h3]

The last few weeks have been very intense and crucial for us, especially with all the high-profile releases surrounding our launch window.

That’s why, if you’d like to support us, the best way is to leave a comment on our YouTube videos, let your friends know about the game, and add the game to your wishlist on Steam.

Next week, you’ll be able to learn more about the world of Dragonkin: The Banished.

Thank you again for all the kind comments; we hope you’re excited for Dragonkin: The Banished!

[h3][b]Feel free to join our Discord[/b][/h3]
We’ll be increasing our presence on Discord over the next few days to gather your feedback and answer your questions. Don’t hesitate to come chat with us and share your thoughts before the Early Access release.

See you soon !

notes.title: Meet the Heroes - Dragonkin: The Banished DevBlog
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/be110b3c2da90b2345f0b1a241ebc6943aa194d0.png[/img]

Today, we’ll be giving you a closer look at the three playable characters you’ll be able to embody in your adventure against the dragons at the start of Early Access:

Electrane the Oracle, Lothair the Knight, and Rurik the Barbarian.

We designed each character with a set of abilities that consume or generate Energy, which you can consider the base resource. The other shared ability is the dodge, designed to get you out of sticky situations.

Additionally, we wanted each hero to have an innate ability thematic to their playstyle that highlights their strengths. This also serves as another resource for players to manage. For the Oracle, her ‘Vision Gauge’ fills with each spell cast and can be used to amplify the power of certain abilities. The Knight’s flamelance gives abilities that make use of his ‘Fuel Gauge’. The Barbarian is fueled by Rage, increasing his damage output and reducing ability cost, but only if he stays in combat, giving him the biggest sense of risk / reward for his playstyle.

[b]Check out our heroes in action in our reveal trailer:[/b]

[previewyoutube=RdJdUC-Hjls;full][/previewyoutube]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/ba9fca1bcb79ed69cff98a55e850560412b842bb.png[/img]

[h3][b]Electrane - The Oracle[/b][/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/fa6d886e9c0924a92242dbbde8f7f0124c66d435.png[/img]

[i]Metamorphosed by the blood of the blue dragon without losing her humanity, she aspires to a world where dragons and humans live in harmony. She uses her electric draconic powers with precision, and can amplify them using her visions.[/i]

[h3][b]Innate Ability: Vision[/b][/h3]

The Oracle's innate ability allows her to consume a portion of her Vision Gauge using a dedicated button to enhance her next ability while reducing its cost. Each ability has a specific upgraded version: projectile bonuses, cooldown reduction, bonus damage, and others you’ll discover in-game, like this rotating laser. This gives players the freedom to choose which ability to upgrade depending on the situation.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/eb9dd1a6cbca4a0cf812570ff5d67643f6a64249.gif[/img]

All skill detail windows in this blog can be clicked for full detail.

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/3664b69bf847d09d17a21ba85dfa017b4f0315f4.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/40bb6f8e479ae921e181fce431df220272ca03c3.png[/img][/url]

[h3][b]Controlling the Battlefield[/b][/h3]

With a combination of slows, stuns, and forced movement abilities, the Oracle has everything she needs to keep enemies far away while avoiding any hits.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/103875f65c26383568ec1b79cfc6b2f68384077c.gif[/img]

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/a359fbac9abba220bfc06669f8f5e55b67e87134.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/35de65a8be1444974875aeea135b66bbaa031f0d.png[/img][/url]

The modifiers in your Ancestral Grid already allow you to customize your abilities. But that's not the only way! The Wyrmling companion that accompanies you also has its own abilities and acts as a specialization, adding effects to abilities that are properly connected in the Ancestral Grid.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/8d10f33f3ae530abc868daa3c321cff69fc90699.gif[/img]

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/44ac29705b29dba7e8b069bc43e1164535ba49a8.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/c31696e9187e366c429ac8af8596c18066528bf9.png[/img][/url]

[h3][b]Blink & Barrier[/b][/h3]

Unlike other Heroes, the Oracle’s Evade is a blink, teleporting a short distance.

A classic in the genre, this instant teleportation allows the Oracle to dodge a powerful attack in a pinch, pass through terrain and enemies, or simply keep her distance.

However, the Oracle remains fragile. This is where the [b]Barrier[/b] stat, shared by all characters, comes into play. The Barrier acts as an additional health bar that regenerates quickly out of combat. It helps save on health potions, but it’s less effective against constant assaults that prevent it from regenerating.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/05a20b32a4573959a991cc51906e1c4cd3a47940.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/bead27dc1e7e8a388ad4ec88768a1908884e8624.png[/img]

[h3][b]Lothair De Montdragon - The Knight[/b][/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/d3d7c37d2692d4417964b07a3ccc927af224976e.png[/img]

[i]Trained in combat from a young age, he masters the fire lance with unparalleled skill. His unwavering faith in the Eternal and his unwavering determination make him impervious to any draconic corruption. He presents himself as the light that will banish darkness![/i]

[h3][b]Innate Ability: Fuel[/b][/h3]

With the Knight, we wanted to highlight equipment and abilities that mirror the power of Dragons—fight fire with fire—making Lothair a Knight unlike any other. Some of his abilities consume Fuel instead of Energy to create fiery effects. This resource passively regenerates over time, though other abilities can restore it. Managing Fuel requires players to carefully alternate their abilities to avoid running out of resources.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/8eb22dbe71bbf8914acede1d8df566fea2598dd9.gif[/img]

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/4faf84e0ba52e25bd00c2d790f80604d9172d317.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/27d4e3836632e63892a9655b4c68282c37b5b158.png[/img][/url]

[h3][b]Armor & Blocking[/b][/h3]

Beyond his offensive abilities and specific resource management, the Knight possesses full armor and a large shield, allowing him to either counterattack or deal damage depending on his defensive potential…

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/33a9d57bb6d77cc55a7093ee200e4d21e6e54f38.gif[/img]

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/73e05ce96dbe14e84cc2184301aa465ac937eb05.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/f834615854e81e014ea619c20424901de1f8c182.png[/img][/url]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/1700068ed5e0d8ee04276ca8dc729f77cadfc63e.gif[/img]

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/4d037f74bc653af9a498aefa56f8ead1d5fb6494.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/df802922df8a4916bfda5223a40386bd364b1da0.png[/img][/url]

There is also a Blocking stat, shared by all heroes, which allows for partial damage mitigation when taking hits.

[h3][b]Support & Summons[/b][/h3]

The Knight also has the ability to support his allies, or summon soldiers to the battlefield, through a banner, passive abilities, or by provoking enemies.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/8426cb10aa17abf45836074b2415099f596a952d.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/b23d67799c0056d324b03eacc41d7d0d96ee9bee.png[/img]

[h3][b]Rurik Haraldson - The Barbarian[/b][/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/965fe56ed4b478c15518b5058a9690cccd42ca5e.png[/img]

[i]Following a dangerous traditional ritual, he became a dragon-blood: half-man, half-monster. His supernatural strength and ice powers combined with legendary rage allow him to defeat the toughest enemies.[/i]

[h3][b]Innate Ability: Rage[/b][/h3]

[i]Following a dangerous traditional ritual, he became a dragon-blood: half-man, half-monster. His supernatural strength and ice powers combined with legendary rage allow him to defeat the toughest enemies.[/i]

Rurik is the very embodiment of rage. With every blow struck or damage taken, his Rage Gauge fills up, allowing him to increase his damage and reduce the cost of his abilities. His rage decreases quickly out of combat, so you’ll need to chain enemies together to maintain a high level of rage and stay at the peak of your power.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/1a34d90355030a1015628c09b5e782cc39ff37e5.gif[/img]

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/f7de1c705bbbc229c991d6bfd7b17297bc4d7772.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/1856e53eb0a3777cb66d19f05b41daf62b1828ba.png[/img][/url]

[h3][b]Moving through the battlefield[/b][/h3]

It was essential to help the Barbarian keep up the pace in order to maintain his rage. That’s why he has high-mobility abilities and mobile attacks, allowing him to chain his enemies together.

Even his dodge ability deals damage to everything he passes through!

notes.title: Dragonkin: The Banished is coming to Early Access on March 6th!
notes.content:
Hello Dragon Hunters!

We are delighted to reveal that [b]Dragonkin: The Banished[/b] is coming out in [b]Early Access[/b] March 6th, 2025 on Steam!

[b]Check out the Early Access trailer[/b] below and come back tomorrow when we’ll be revealing a new developer diary with a look at more gameplay for Dragonkin: The Banished.

[previewyoutube=GZplLwKdess;full][/previewyoutube]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/7ee8d6fa692acb343f59d6adb6acacd9cf889380.png[/img]
[h3][b]So, why Early Access, you ask?[/b][/h3]

[b]At Eko Software[/b], we’re a small but passionate team of around 30 people working on Dragonkin: The Banished. We’re crazy about the ARPG genre, particularly Hack & Slash games. We’ve been making them for around 12 years now!

[b]For Dragonkin: The Banished[/b], we wanted to push the boundaries of what we’ve done before. We moved development to Unreal Engine 5, allowing us more flexibility compared to our previous engine. One of our goals is to highlight the things we love about the genre while bringing in something fresh and new to delight fans.

[b]For the launch of Early Access[/b] on March 6th, we have prepared content to introduce you to the world of Dragonkin. You can play through the prologue and 1st act as one of 3 classes, collect gear, and expand your skills using the Ancestral Grid. You’ll have access to a couple of end game modes and be able to start levelling up your city. We think it’s a good starting point, but there’s more to come.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/7574351fc687ec30ff06eb9300c00c73cff266c3.png[/img]

[b]We’ll be bolstering[/b] this content throughout until launch with what’s planned on our roadmap. Expect regular updates including the addition of online multiplayer and more character skills, biomes, the addition of the 4th character and more endgame content. It also has room for us to make adjustments and tweaks to address player feedback and concerns. We’ll publish more information on the roadmap prior to launch, so keep an eye out for that.

[b]Within the ARPG genre[/b], we believe there is ample room for innovation and one of our major goals involves the Ancestral Grid which we’re going to deep-dive in a future Dev Blog. But the general idea incorporates randomly generated fragments that are collected as you play, ensuring that by the end of the journey, your grid will be completely unique. We wanted to add an element of fun while making your grid, while giving theory-crafters the flexibility to adapt their grids and come up with new playstyles.

[b]Early Access is a collaborative process[/b]. We know how passionate the ARPG community is, and want to get as much feedback from our players as possible. We’ll be using this to shape and improve the game as we move towards the 1.0 launch. Early Access also gives us the opportunity to invest further into the project, possibly altering or expanding the scope of our plans for Dragonkin: The Banished.

We have many goals for development, but being in Early Access gives us the opportunity to bring the community into the process and we strongly believe that it will result in a better version of the game for everyone.

[h3][b]How to support us?[/b][/h3]

Share the trailer, spread the word, and [b]wishlisting[/b] Dragonkin: The Banished on Steam helps us a lot!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1863430/Dragonkin_The_Banished/


[h3][b]What's next?[/b][/h3]

We’ve got a lot to share in the coming weeks, starting with a [b]Developer Diary tomorrow (January 10th)[/b], where we’ll discuss some of the systems and gameplay in Dragonkin: The Banished.

In the meantime, don’t hesitate to join us on social media and Discord if you haven’t yet, for the latest news, discussions, and exclusive sneak peeks. Know that your enthusiasm and support mean the world to us, and we’re so grateful to have you on this journey.

[b]Happy New Year from the team at Eko Software, and get ready for our next DevBlog![/b]

notes.title: Welcome to Ja'Ksara - Dragonkin: The Banished Dev Blog
notes.content:
Hello Hunters!

In this blog, we want to give you an exclusive first look into the world of [i]Dragonkin: The Banished[/i]. As you may know from our [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1863430/view/4459221603601874983]class blog[/url], Dragon Blood can have various effects, granting immense power, but often at a deep cost.

For you to better understand the insidious nature of the blood seeping into the world itself, we’ll walk you through two areas within one of the biome’s you’ll step into, a place twisted and tainted by Green Dragon Blood: the [i]Jungle[/i] and the [i]Swamps of Ja'Ksara[/i].

Let’s dive in!

[b][h2]The Swamps of Ja'Ksara[/h2][/b]

This treacherous land is home to the [b]Toxic Dragons[/b], whose blood has had a disturbing, corrupting effect on everything it touches. From the wildlife to the vegetation, the swamp is a twisted reflection of the [b]Green Dragon’s[/b] power.

As you venture through the swamp, you’ll come across Batrachians that release deadly toxins when threatened, monstrous Moths that unleash swarms of insects ready to overwhelm you, Leeches (oh god, the leeches!) and Shamans that wield the electrical powers of the Blue Dragon, just to name a few.

After all, who truly knows what else may lurk beneath these muddied waters…

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/1ca6d75fcccbff93a84d276f328b6cb020700120.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/eea6f735a3ba312f74cc47da525623255d435f50.png[/img]

Nestled within the towering treetops, you’ll discover a [b]cult village[/b]. Here the tainted waters have even begun to affect the locals.

[h3][b]Meet the Monstrous Swarm[/b][/h3]

Without a doubt you’ll meet the [b]Monstrous Swarm[/b], a [i]moth-like[/i] (and terrifying creature) that has been completely transformed by Green Dragon blood. Characterized by it’s enormous mouth, it can summon [b]Dragonflies[/b], tiny but deadly insects, ready to sting on sight.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/182d331babec308b777c0e09857a02a8dfd74e4c.gif[/img]

[h2][b]The Jungle of Ja'Ksara[/b][/h2]

While the Jungle may appear peaceful, especially at night, these decayed ruins are far from deserted. Corrupted creatures wander, hostile to those who dare venture too close to their homes.  And as you journey deeper, the Jungle itself will threaten your progress, as if [i]something[/i] doesn't want you to reach its core.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/a3b939d2e9119798dd7e4c35c1fd538cfe563320.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/f37ed023260ee52ea7850ae1cf12f3edf9bcc132.png[/img]

Despite the Jungle being viciously dangerous and inhospitable, the serene sight of waterfalls reminds us of the world the warriors are trying to protect as you uncover the mysteries hidden under the roots.

[h3][b]Meet the Rampant Corruption[/b][/h3]

It’s here in the Jungle that you'll cross paths with this unnatural [i]rampant tree-like[/i] creature animated by the Blood of the Green Dragon.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/8e220815f0aa60b8639d5f6b2f4fe7fdc87545ec.gif[/img]

[b][h2]We hope this sneak peek at [i]Dragonkin: The Banished[/i] has you even more excited for the adventure ahead![/h2][/b]

[b]What are you most excited to explore, the Swamps or the Jungle?[/b]
Let us know in the comments, or hop into our [url=https://discord.gg/RDuhVMj4]Discord server[/url] to discuss it with fellow hunters!

We’ll be back soon with more updates, so stay tuned!

notes.title: Sneak Peek at some of the Dragonkin roster!
notes.content:
Hello future Dragon Hunters, 

Over the past few weeks, we've been sharing some snippets on our [url=https://discord.gg/cQqSMMMh57]developer discord[/url] (yes, that is a shameless plug). Since these are usually small teasers, we won't post everything there onto Steam - we wouldn't want to flood the channels. 

However, when appropriate, we'll bring these assets together and share them as part of larger pieces like the one you're reading right now! 

So, without further ado. We're going to give you a very quick introduction to some of the playable characters in Dragonkin. We're planning to deep-dive into their character, playstyle, itemization, and abilities later on, so definitely stay tuned for that! 

[h3]Knight[/h3]
The Knight is a stalwart defender, trained in combat from a young age to master the Dragon Lance. He usually is the first to charge into combat, but mechanical innovations to his lance allow it to bellow out fire to keep the enemy hordes at bay. While this may look rather draconic, the Knight eschews all forms of draconic corruption, instead fueled by his powerful faith in the Eternal and strict moral code. 

[previewyoutube=TCrE59pE2h8;full][/previewyoutube]
[h3]Oracle[/h3]
The caste that the Oracle hails from have been transformed by the power of blue dragon blood. It's a power that imbues her people with powerful electric abilities. Ultimately, she dreams of a realm where humans and dragon can live side by side, but knows that dangerous Dragons must be fought off to achieve that.

[previewyoutube=NxDQYVLC7So;full][/previewyoutube]
[h3]Barbarian[/h3]
The hardiest of the Barbarian who survive the ritual of ingesting White Dragon Blood can harness its power of ice. The dragon's blood mingles with their own, granting these warriors a supernatural strength that makes them more powerful as long as they remain in battle.

[previewyoutube=gZZNU06YfGo;full][/previewyoutube]
We'll have more to share on these heroes, and on the Tracker in the future. Please check out our social channels to stay up to date on everything related to Dragonkin: The Banished. We'll be back shortly hunters, but until then stay ready.

notes.title: Welcome to the Dragonkin: The Banished Devblog!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44904587/c38a564bc7bc7087e61d24d6114e41e6acfdd259.png[/img]

After the last updates to Chaosbane nearly 4 years ago, we took our first steps working with Unreal Engine 4. A few months later, we began drafting the first elements of the universe and game design for [b]our next ARPG project, which would eventually become Dragonkin: The Banished[/b]. After several months of pre-production, this time on [b]Unreal 5[/b], we officially started production around 3 years ago. 

Today, we're excited to welcome you to the very first devblog in a series that will allow us to share more and more about the development of our new Hack & Slash. It’s intended to share our progress and ideas as we move through the final stages of development on Dragonkin, a project that has been a passion of ours for several years now. 

[h3]But what is Dragonkin? [/h3]
Dragonkin is a Hack & Slash set in a completely original universe created by our team. Unlike our previous Hack & Slash, Chaosbane, which was based on an existing universe, [b]Dragonkin takes place in a brand-new world[/b], though one deeply rooted in a theme we love: medieval fantasy (with spoiler alert, dragons!). 

We’re deep into production, with about 30 people actively working on the project. Various elements like graphics, gameplay, UI, game systems, animations, visual effects, sounds, and even music are starting to come together, and the game is beginning to take shape. This is an exciting time for us, as we’ll be able to reveal more about the game in the coming weeks and months. 

In upcoming posts, we’ll share more details about different aspects of the game: its universe, theory crafting, itemization, enemies, playable characters, and more. For now, we’re excited to share this first visual of our armored Knight! 

[previewyoutube=TCrE59pE2h8;full][/previewyoutube]
See you soon in the world of Dragonkin and if you want to hear more directly from the team come join our [url=https://discord.gg/cQqSMMMh57]official Discord![/url]

The Eko Software team
